spans.quote: I didn't keep to the routine every morning, either: on two mornings, I skipped reading altogether.
The change I noticed was in how I read: I stopped interrupting a chapter to check messages.

findings.observation: The 'either' has a loose connection to the preceding phone-checking sentence, because checking after finishing complied with the routine. Dropping 'either' would make that transition cleaner, but the explicit two skipped mornings and every-morning qualification prevent a material misstatement. This states the behavioral difference plainly; the source's modest evaluative word 'simpler' is less explicit. The underlying contrast and personal approval remain.
findings.interpretation: This is a local editorial observation, not a diagnostic authorship cue. AI rewriting can produce this organization or connective choice; the score-independent source comparison, not a detector explanation, supports this finding.
findings.human_alternative: A human reflective writer can use the same modest self-assessment, short personal reaction and imperfect connective. Neither experience-like detail nor minor awkwardness establishes a lived event or human origin.
findings.discriminating_evidence: Compare alternative wording with the unchanged source and ask independent readers about the actual audience. Authenticated process records, rather than this stylistic feature, would distinguish writing histories.

paragraph_reviews.text: For eight weeks, I read a chapter in the morning before looking at my phone, expecting to remember more of what I read. By the end, I could recall the plots of three novels. But I hadn't tested my memory before the experiment, so I can't tell whether my recall improved.
